events.what: Explicit degree-23 polynomial over Q with Galois group M23, completing realization of all 26 sporadic simple groups
events.ai_basis: We used Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol for searching the literature, code generation, testing hypotheses, ruling out other approaches, devising computational strategies, checking our results, and proofreading our manuscript.

judgement.doubts: Scope is clearly a case (one finite group of the bullet's 'every finite group'); the polynomial is explicit and was verified in Magma and PARI/GP, so verification is checkable, though tier is partial regardless. The ai_role assisted/none boundary is genuinely close: the paper's own list is mostly auxiliary tasks, but the co-author blog as summarised in the record says AI produced the initial numerical approximations of the Belyi map data that were later recognised via PSLQ as the coefficients, i.e. part of the computation whose output is in the final polynomial. Kept assisted on that basis.

corrections.why: F9: kept with doubt. The paper's acknowledgements list mostly non-credited uses (literature search, checking, proofreading), but per the record's summary of the co-author blog, AI produced the numerical approximations of the Belyi map data later recognised as the polynomial's algebraic coefficients, which is mathematics in the result; 'devising computational strategies' alone would not suffice.
